title: SPERA: Spherical Prior EEG Foundation Model with Geometry- and Frequency-Aware Latent Prediction
claim: A latent-prediction pretraining pipeline, built from geometry-aware tokenization, hybrid attention and a spectral regularizer, learns general representations from heterogeneous signals.
layout: 4 quadrants, left-to-right flows, color-coded modules, nested encoder and regularizer boxes
description: A four-quadrant diagram with orange section headings. Top-left shows input EEG (channels C by time T) being cut into non-overlapping 1 s patches. Some patches are masked and shaded orange as targets, and the rest are context patches. Top-right shows tokenization. Channel coordinates (x, y, z) and raw patches go through linear embeddings and are combined into tokens. Bottom-left is the main pretraining framework. A green box holds a teacher encoder and a student encoder, linked by an EMA arrow. A cross-attention predictor outputs predicted target latents, and the JEPA loss compares these with stop-gradient target latents. A grey box labelled relational spectral regularizer compares cosine-similarity matrices of the latents with those of the log-power spectrum, using KL divergence. The total loss is L = L_JEPA + λL_spec. Bottom-right shows the encoder architecture. Hybrid attention blocks combine factorized temporal and spatial attention with periodic full attention. A blue box shows the Legendre spherical prior, built on a head diagram with electrode angles, feeding attention bias and query/key.
caption: Overview of the SPERA pretraining framework.
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive measure of ongoing neural activity, but building general-purpose EEG models remains challenging due to the heterogeneity of subjects, devices, and electrode montages. Existing EEG foundation models predominantly rely on reconstruction-based objectives defined on the observed signal, which contains both neural and non-neural components. We introduce the Spherical Prior EEG Representation Architecture (SPERA), an EEG foundation model that adopts the joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to predict in latent space. SPERA introduces a Legendre-polynomial spatial prior, incorporated into attention to encode varying scalp electrode geometries. Two further components adapt the model to EEG: factorized temporal and spatial attention interleaved with periodic full-attention blocks, and a relational spectral regularizer aligning latent similarity structure with spectral views. Pretrained on approximately 80,000 hours of EEG from 29,048 subjects across 106 datasets, SPERA achieves the highest average balanced accuracy across nine downstream tasks spanning clinical, cognitive, and BCI applications. SPERA further exhibits strong parameter efficiency under linear probing and robustness across varying recording conditions, suggesting its potential as a general-purpose backbone for diverse EEG analyses.
